title: Python 3.15.0 Beta 2 Release Announcement
summary: Python 3.15.0 Beta 2 has been released as part of the beta phase for Python 3.15. This pre-release is intended for testing new features, bug fixes, and preparing third-party projects for the upcoming stable release. Key changes include performance improvements, new built-in types, enhanced profiling tools, and UTF-8 as the default encoding. The release is not recommended for production environments.
key_points: Python 3.15.0 Beta 2 is the second of four planned beta releases for Python 3.15.
Beta releases are for community testing of new features and bug fixes before the stable release.

Major new features include: PEP 810 (lazy imports), PEP 814 (frozendict), PEP 661 (sentinel type), PEP 799 (profiling package and Tachyon profiler), PEP 831 (frame pointers enabled by default), and UTF-8 as the default encoding (PEP 686).
Performance improvements: 8-9% speedup on x86-64 Linux and 12-13% on AArch64 macOS due to JIT compiler upgrades and tail-calling interpreter optimizations.
Windows 64-bit binaries now use the tail-calling interpreter for better performance.
New stable ABI for free-threaded builds and related C API improvements.
Features may still change or be removed before the release candidate phase (2026-08-04).
Third-party project maintainers are encouraged to test with 3.15 and report issues.
Production use is discouraged until the release candidate (3.15.0rc1).
